text:
The Canadiens have a point in twelve straight games (9-0-3) and sit at 12-3-4. It was a big week off the ice too: Carey Price, a day after his Hall of Fame induction, got a four-minute standing ovation at the Bell Centre as he joined the Ring of Honour.

Here is the honest part. Martin St-Louis's team has earned about half of the expected goals (49%, the quality of chances for and against) during the streak and all season. What separates the record from the process is goaltending: Montreal has allowed almost nine fewer goals than its chances predicted, and Jacob Fowler has saved 3.6 goals above expected over his last five starts (3-0-2). Our numbers have the Canadiens about eight points ahead of what their play deserves, with a 72% chance at the playoffs.

The bright spots are real. Phillip Danault, Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc have taken 61% of the expected goals together, and Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson run a 58% pair. The worry is the penalty box: nearly five minors a game against about four drawn, which makes Cole Caufield's complaints about the referees and the scrutiny on Arber Xhekaj more than talk-radio noise. Sportsnet's Eric Engels called entry defense a work in progress, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking agrees: opponents carry the puck in 47% of the time. Juraj Slafkovský (5 points in 10, 7.5 expected) is due some puck luck.
headline: Twelve straight with a point, and a goalie behind it
